findings.description: Static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, making them readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration and committing them to version control.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here hold credentials) are protected only by the AWS-managed default key, with no customer control of key policy, rotation, or usage auditing.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a deprecated Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group control, providing an unmonitored data exfiltration path.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-validated and tampering between build and deployment would not be detected.

The execution role is created without a permissions_boundary, so there is no guardrail capping the privileges that can later be attached to the role used by an internet-facing function holding static credentials.

The trust policy allows the entire lambda.amazonaws.com service principal to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, which permits cross-account confused-deputy assumption paths.
